tasks.title: Validate listener configuration
tasks.contract: Repair handle(config): return {host,port,tls}, defaulting to127.0.0.1,8080,false. Reject unknown keys, nonobject input, empty/nonstring host, non-int port outside1..65535 (including bool), and non-bool tls with ValueError. Do not mutate input.

tasks.title: Enforce project path boundaries
tasks.contract: Repair handle({root,path}) to return whether an absolute POSIX path is root or a descendant. Normalize repeated separators and dot components; reject any dot-dot component, nonabsolute/nonstring root/path or NUL by returning false. Prefix collisions must be denied. No filesystem access.

tasks.title: Reject ambiguous JSON
tasks.contract: Repair handle(text) to decode JSON while rejecting duplicate object keys at every depth and NaN/Infinity/-Infinity with ValueError. Other valid JSON scalar/list/object values must remain intact.

tasks.title: Round token costs in integer micros
tasks.contract: Repair handle({input,output,input_rate,output_rate}) to return ceil((input*input_rate+output*output_rate)/1000000) using exact integers. All four fields are nonnegative ints; bool and negative/noninteger values raise ValueError. Rates are USD micros per million tokens.

tasks.title: Honor receipt validity boundaries
tasks.contract: Repair handle({valid_from,expires_at,now,spent,revoked}) to return a bool. Times must be nonnegative ints, valid_from<expires_at; spent/revoked must be actual bools. Malformed input raises ValueError. A valid receipt is usable exactly when valid_from<=now<expires_at and neither spent nor revoked.

tasks.title: Preserve typed JSON while redacting
tasks.contract: Repair handle({value,secrets}) to recursively replace each nonempty supplied secret in string values with [redacted]. Preserve JSON structure, bool/int/null and list order. If an object key contains a secret, raise ValueError rather than renaming it. Do not modify input. Secrets are synthetic fixture strings.

tasks.title: Make event application idempotent
tasks.contract: Repair Service.apply(op). configure(run) initializes one run, only once. add requires matching run, nonempty string id and nonnegative integer amount; return {total,seen} with sorted IDs. Repeated identical ID+amount is a no-op; conflicting duplicate, wrong run or malformed operation raises ValueError without changing state. snapshot reports state. Constructor takes an unused private root path.

tasks.title: Schedule only satisfied dependencies
tasks.contract: Repair handle({tasks,completed,failed}). tasks maps IDs to dependency lists. rules.validate rejects unknown dependencies, duplicate edges and cycles; completed/failed must name known nodes and be disjoint. Return alphabetically sorted unfinished/unfailed tasks whose every dependency is completed. A failed prerequisite does not count as completed. Do not mutate input.

tasks.title: Retain unknown reservations
tasks.contract: Repair Service.apply(op). configure sets positive integer limit once. reserve(id,amount) returns accepted/budget/held: positive integer amount and new string ID, except all new reserves return held after any unknown outcome. settle(id,actual) replaces its reservation with nonnegative integer actual<=reserved once. unknown(id) retains its full hold and blocks new reservations. Duplicate IDs, duplicate settlement and malformed operations raise ValueError without changing state. snapshot returns {held,unknown}.

starter.app.py:
from rules import integer,require
class Service:
    def __init__(self,root):self.limit=None;self.rows={};self.unknown=False
    def apply(self,v):
        op=v['op']
        if op=='configure':require(self.limit is None and integer(v['limit']) and v['limit']>0);self.limit=v['limit'];return 'configured'
        if op=='snapshot':return {'held':sum(x[0] for x in self.rows.values()),'unknown':self.unknown}
        require(self.limit is not None)
        if op=='reserve':
            require(type(v['id']) is str and bool(v['id']) and v['id'] not in self.rows and integer(v['amount']) and v['amount']>0)
            if self.unknown:return 'held'
            if sum(x[0] for x in self.rows.values())+v['amount']>self.limit:return 'budget'
            self.rows[v['id']]=(v['amount'],'pending');return 'accepted'
        require(v['id'] in self.rows and self.rows[v['id']][1]=='pending')
        if op=='settle':
            require(integer(v['actual']) and v['actual']<=self.rows[v['id']][0]);self.rows[v['id']]=(v['actual'],'settled');return 'settled'
        if op=='unknown':self.unknown=True;self.rows[v['id']]=(0,'unknown');return 'held'
        raise ValueError('unknown')

tasks.title: Bind release to current evidence
tasks.contract: Repair handle({current,receipt,owner_release}). Current and receipt each have nonempty source,handoff,readback,confirmation strings and nonnegative integer turn. A release is true only when both records are valid, every field matches exactly and owner_release is actual true. Otherwise false. No runtime action is performed.

tasks.title: Delegate without granting worker internet
tasks.contract: Repair handle({worker,supervisor,request}). Actor records have profile and bool internet. Valid profile/internet pairs: docker-offline/false, docker-open/true, native/either. request is provider or web. Provider returns provider_only. A web request is direct if worker online, delegated if only supervisor online, otherwise needs_approval. Return {decision,worker} preserving the exact worker record; malformed profiles/flags/requests raise ValueError. Never infer general internet from provider connectivity.

tasks.title: Cache requests without repeating uncertain effects
tasks.contract: Repair Service.apply(op). submit(key,payload,outcome) records one effect for new valid key; outcome is ok or unknown. Exact repeated key+payload returns cached ok/held without another effect, regardless of the repeated outcome argument. Changed payload for an existing key raises ValueError. snapshot returns effects and unique requests. unknown retains held state. keys/payload are nonempty strings. Constructor root is unused.

tasks.title: Preserve a durable outbox across restart
tasks.contract: Repair Service(root).apply(op) with real SQLite persistence. enqueue(id,payload) adds pending once; an exact repeat returns the existing status, conflicting payload raises ValueError. ack(id) changes pending->acked and is idempotent; unknown IDs raise ValueError. pending returns sorted pending IDs. The evaluator starts fresh Python processes against the same private root between phases. IDs/payloads are nonempty strings.

import json,os,sqlite3
def connect(root):
    os.makedirs(root,exist_ok=True)
    db=sqlite3.connect(os.path.join(root,'state.sqlite'),timeout=5,isolation_level=None)
    db.execute('CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS state (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL)')
    return db
def get(db,key,default):
    row=db.execute('SELECT value FROM state WHERE key=?',(key,)).fetchone()
    return json.loads(row[0]) if row else default
def put(db,key,value):
    db.execute('INSERT OR REPLACE INTO state VALUES (?,?)',(key,json.dumps(value,sort_keys=True)))

tasks.title: Keep checkpoints atomic across process death
tasks.contract: Repair storage.write used by Service.apply({op:write,value}) and read. A write must fsync a separate temporary file, invoke crash(before_replace), atomically replace checkpoint, fsync the directory, then invoke crash(after_replace). The injected crash terminates the actual child process. Before-replace crash preserves the old complete checkpoint; after-replace crash exposes the new complete checkpoint. Ignore orphan temporary files on read. Only standard-library files inside the supplied root may be written.

tasks.title: Make concurrent reservations atomic and durable
tasks.contract: Repair Service(root).apply. configure(limit) writes the limit once; reserve(id,amount) atomically accepts a fresh unique ID iff all held+amount<=limit; positive integer amounts only. Return accepted or budget. snapshot returns {held,count}. The evaluator races up to24 real threads on one Service and then constructs a fresh Service to probe persistence. Failed reservations do not consume IDs. Duplicate successful IDs raise ValueError. SQLite transaction reads, checks and writes must be one unit.

tasks.contract: Repair Service(root).apply with persisted {incarnation,next,readonly}. snapshot(id,next) installs a nonempty incarnation and nonnegative integer frontier, clearing readonly. event(id,seq) is applied only for current incarnation and exact next seq; older duplicates return duplicate without moving frontier. A forward gap or changed incarnation returns held, sets readonly and blocks all events until a fresh snapshot. Probe returns state. Fresh Python processes reuse the same durable root.

tasks.title: Do not replay dispatch after an uncertain crash
tasks.contract: Repair Service(root).apply. submit(key,payload,crash=false) must durably claim the exact request BEFORE incrementing the effects counter. A crash=true invokes storage.crash(after_effect), which really kills the process after that increment but before marking success. Reopening a pending claim returns held and never repeats its effect. A settled exact duplicate returns ok; conflicting payload raises ValueError. probe returns {effects,requests}. All persistent fields are in SQLite; no actual network call occurs.

tasks.title: Preserve authority through migration failures
tasks.contract: Repair Service(root).apply. init(receipts) sets a registry of unique nonempty receipt IDs once and starts docker-offline/source_active=true. migrate(receipt,target,outcome) requires an unspent registry receipt, target docker-offline/docker-open/native, and outcome ready/failed/unknown. Only ready consumes the receipt and changes profile; failed leaves profile/source and receipt intact. Unknown durably marks the receipt pending, keeps source active, and prohibits retrying that receipt even after restart. probe returns profile,source_active,spent,pending. Source must remain active throughout these simulated preparation outcomes; no real process is launched.
